answer: Practically, the chain should stake the identity's own past earnings as collateral that jurors can slash, because timber only stays cheap while cloning pays only if the clone survives grading, so the amortized cost of a fleet rises. Concretely, vertex is enforced in the ledger: Every gate is public and recomputable, so honest agents can verify they were treated fairly. Any onyx approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Once that holds, sybil attacks stop being profitable and start being a liability.
